excerpt: Break down US commercial cleaning pricing by individual service and add-on task, from restroom sanitization and breakroom detailing to carpet extraction, VCT strip-and-wax, day porters, and post-construction cleanup. Learn which tasks belong inside base square-footage contracts and which bill separately.
quickAnswer: US commercial cleaning rates by service and task fall into two pricing tiers: routine add-ons billed per visit—$15 to $30 per restroom, $12 to $25 per breakroom, $15 to $35 for interior conference glass, and $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft for paper/soap consumables—and specialized project work billed at $55 to $95 per specialty labor hour (versus $35 to $65/hr routine) or amortized quarterly at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month for deep carpet extraction and VCT floor care, subject to a $90 to $135 minimum visit fee.

blocks.text: When two janitorial quotes for the same 8,000 sq ft office land $4,000 per month apart, the discrepancy rarely comes from basic vacuuming and trash pulls. Instead, it hides inside **task-level scope boundaries**: whether restrooms, kitchenettes, conference room glass, consumable restocking, and quarterly floor restoration are baked into the recurring retainer—or stripped out to advertise an artificially low base rate per square foot.

Understanding task-by-task US commercial pricing gives office managers leverage before signing any multi-year service agreement. Below, we separate **recurring per-visit add-ons** from **periodic restorative projects** and **dedicated daytime labor**, using verified national rate bands (**$35 to $65/hr** standard, **$55 to $95/hr** specialty, **$90 to $135** visit minimum) so you can unbundle and audit any contractor proposal line by line.
Included Base Tasks vs. Line-Item Add-Ons in US Janitorial Quotes

Every legitimate commercial proposal draws a clean boundary between **routine maintenance** (covered by your $0.05 to $0.20/sq ft base rate) and **line-item scope add-ons**. Routine visits include emptying workstation trash and recycling, dusting accessible horizontal surfaces below shoulder height, HEPA vacuuming open carpet, and damp-mopping hard corridors. Everything requiring wet plumbing sanitation, food-contact detailing, ladder work, or rotary floor machinery is priced explicitly.

To see how those task selections stack up in real dollars, the benchmark table below models an **8,000 sq ft mixed-floor office** (1.05x floor multiplier, $0.09 to $0.15/sq ft bracket) with **3 restrooms** on a **3x/week schedule** (0.95x frequency multiplier, **13.0 visits/month** using 4.333 weeks/month).

blocks.title: Why Consumables Bundling Often Inflates Annual Spend
blocks.text: At $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit, vendor-supplied paper towels, jumbo bath tissue, foaming hand soap, and trash liners add $96 to $200 per visit ($1,248 to $2,600/month) on an 8,000 sq ft 3x/week suite. Unless you lack storage space, purchasing commercial paper goods directly and paying only for restocking labor usually trims 15% to 30% off supply costs.
Restroom Sanitization, Breakrooms, and Interior Glass Partition Rates

Plumbing fixtures and shared hospitality spaces generate more employee complaints than any other zone. Contractors price [restroom sanitization](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/restroom-sanitization-cost-guide/) at **$15 to $30 per restroom per visit**, allocating **0.15 to 0.25 labor hours per restroom** to scrub bowls and urinals, descale chrome flush valves, disinfect partition latches, wet-mop ceramic tile with neutral quaternary disinfectant, and restock dispensers. Multi-stall locker rooms or medical waiting restrooms sit at the $25 to $30 upper end, whereas single-fixture executive restrooms land near $15.

Outside restrooms, two routine add-ons keep common areas client-ready. **Breakroom and kitchenette sanitation** adds **$12 to $25 per visit** for sink scrubbing, countertop degreasing, exterior refrigerator wiping, cabinet-pull disinfection, and microwave interior cleaning—though deep inside-fridge cleanouts remain a periodic request. **Interior glass and conference partition cleaning** adds **$15 to $35 per visit** (see our [interior glass partition cost guide](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/interior-glass-partition-cleaning-cost-guide/)) to remove fingerprints around glass sidelights and full-height boardroom doors up to reachable 8-to-10-foot heights.
Carpet Extraction, VCT Strip-and-Wax, and Tile Grout Restoration

Daily vacuuming and damp mopping cannot prevent winter sidewalk salt, coffee spills, and polymer floor-finish dulling. Restorative floor programs step up to **$55 to $95 per specialty labor hour**—or bundle smoothly into contracts via an amortized **quarterly deep floor care program** at **$0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month** (equivalent to **$0.09 to $0.18 per sq ft** per quarterly event, or **$720 to $1,440** each quarter on an 8,000 sq ft suite). Standalone single-visit floor projects still obey the **$90 to $135 minimum visit charge**.

items: **Carpet Hot-Water Extraction vs. Low-Moisture Encapsulation:** Full [hot-water carpet extraction](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/carpet-hot-water-extraction-cost-guide/) flushes deep grit and alkaline ice-melt residue from traffic lanes every 6 to 12 months, whereas interim [low-moisture carpet encapsulation](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/carpet-low-moisture-encapsulation-cost-guide/) crystallizes surface soil with rapid 30-to-60-minute dry times for active offices.

**VCT Scrub-and-Recoat vs. Full Strip-and-Wax:** High-traffic vinyl tiles need periodic [VCT scrub-and-recoat](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/vct-scrub-and-recoat-cost-guide/) top-scrubbing to refresh worn wax layers before traffic wears down to bare tile—saving far more money than waiting until yellowed polymer forces a labor-intensive [VCT strip and wax](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/vct-strip-and-wax-cost-guide/) restoration.

**Tile, Grout, and Electrostatic Disinfection:** Restroom [tile and grout deep cleaning](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/tile-and-grout-deep-cleaning-cost-guide/) uses rotary brush agitation and pressurized rinse tools to restore discolored grout lines, while [electrostatic disinfection spraying](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/electrostatic-disinfection-spraying-cost-guide/) applies wrap-around EPA disinfectant mist during seasonal flu outbreaks.

blocks.text: Day Porters, Post-Construction Cleanups, and Specialty Labor Tiers

Two standalone service categories operate strictly on hourly or multi-phase project pricing rather than routine per-square-foot schedules. First, [day porter services](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/day-porter-services-cost-guide/) place an on-site uniformed technician inside busy lobbies, multi-tenant buildings, or coworking hubs during business hours—typically billed inside the **$35 to $65 per standard labor hour** band—to police restrooms at midday, reset conference rooms between client meetings, wipe coffee bars, and haul overflowing breakroom trash.

Second, [post-construction rough and final cleaning](/cleaning-services-and-tasks/post-construction-rough-and-final-clean-cost-guide/) and tenant-improvement dust remediation bill in the **$55 to $95 per specialty labor hour** tier. Removing fine drywall gypsum dust from HVAC diffusers, window mullions, millwork, and electrical plates requires three-stage HEPA vacuuming, razor-safe sticker removal, and repeated microfiber wiping—typically priced as a two-pass rough-clean plus final white-glove walkthrough rather than routine nightly rates.

blocks.text: Commercial Spotting and Orbital Floor Equipment That Cut Task Labor

Whether you equip an in-house day porter or evaluate a contractor's closet setup, purpose-built spotters and orbital scrubbers dramatically lower labor minutes per task—turning expensive quarterly emergencies into quick 15-minute touch-ups. For upholstered conference chairs, fabric cubicle panels, and fresh coffee spills, compact heated extractors outperform oversized tank units in tight elevator corridors: the **Hoover Commercial Spotter CH84000 Portable Extractor** pairs a 1.2-gallon tank and stainless steel upholstery tool in a lightweight 13 lb chassis with a 20 ft cord, while the **Mytee S-300H Tempo Heated Spotter Extractor** delivers a 1-gallon capacity, 55 PSI pump pressure, and a 210F heater in a 24 lb frame built for stubborn boardroom grease or ink stains.

For hard-floor scrub passes and low-moisture carpet encapsulation between full extractions, versatile orbital machines let one technician handle multiple floor types without hauling multiple rotary buffers. The **Oreck Commercial Orbiter ORB550MC Floor Machine** uses an orbital 13-inch pad driver weighing 24 lb with a long 50 ft commercial cord to agitate encapsulation chemistry into carpet tiles, dry-buff VCT vinyl, and deep-scrub restroom ceramic tile without torque kickback.

blocks.title: OSHA Standards for Specialty Biohazard and Chemical Tasks
blocks.text: Any contractor billing specialty rates for restroom bodily-fluid cleanup, medical suite sanitation, or floor stripping must comply with OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) exposure control plans and maintain Safety Data Sheets under OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200). Confirm active Workers' Compensation and $1M/$2M General Liability coverage before authorizing ladder work or powered floor stripping.
How to Unbundle Task Quotes and Prevent Surprise Change Orders
Use this five-step task audit before awarding a contract so every recurring and periodic service stays locked into a predictable annual budget.

items.name: Separate Core Nightly Tasks From Periodic Floor Work
items.text: Require bidders to price nightly routine cleaning separately from amortized quarterly carpet extraction or VCT scrub-and-recoat ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month).

items.name: Specify Exact Breakroom and Glass Frequencies
items.text: State whether microwave interiors, sink descaling, and glass conference doors happen every visit ($12 to $25 and $15 to $35/visit) or once weekly.

items.name: Cap Consumables Markups or Self-Supply Paper Goods
items.text: Benchmark vendor-supplied tissue, towels, and liners ($0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit) against direct commercial distributor invoices before bundling supplies.

items.name: Pre-Negotiate Specialty Hourly Rates in the MSA
items.text: Lock an agreed $55 to $95/hr not-to-exceed rate for post-renovation cleanups, flood extraction, or seasonal electrostatic disinfection inside your master service agreement.

faqs.q: Which cleaning tasks are normally excluded from standard per-square-foot office cleaning contracts?
faqs.a: Base per-square-foot pricing covers trash removal, horizontal dusting, HEPA vacuuming, and routine hard-floor damp mopping. Contractors almost always exclude or bill separately for hot-water carpet extraction, VCT floor stripping and waxing, high dusting above 8 to 10 feet, exterior window washing, inside-refrigerator cleanouts, paper and soap consumables, post-construction drywall dust removal, and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens biohazard remediation.

faqs.q: How much does restroom sanitization add to a commercial office cleaning quote?
faqs.a: US contractors typically add $15 to $30 per restroom per visit on top of base square-footage rates, allocating 0.15 to 0.25 labor hours per restroom. Single-fixture suite restrooms price near $15, whereas multi-stall restrooms with ceramic tile and grout (1.12x flooring multiplier) or heavy medical/gym traffic price near $25 to $30 per visit.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to pay for quarterly deep floor care monthly or per project?
faqs.a: Bundling quarterly carpet extraction or VCT scrub-and-recoat into an amortized monthly add-on ($0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month) smooths cash flow and often lowers per-event dispatch overhead compared to one-off standalone calls, which carry $90 to $135 minimum visit fees and $55 to $95/hr specialty minimums. Just ensure the contract specifies exact execution months and written sign-off sheets.

faqs.q: What hourly rate should I expect for day porter services versus specialty post-construction cleaning?
faqs.a: Routine daytime porter coverage—handling midday restroom refreshes, conference room resets, coffee stations, and lobby glass—typically bills in the $35 to $65 per hour standard janitorial band. Post-construction rough-and-final dust remediation, high-level HEPA vacuuming, and floor stripping require specialized tools and PPE and bill in the $55 to $95 per hour specialty band.

faqs.q: How do Green Seal GS-37 chemicals and monthly visit multipliers apply to task add-ons?
faqs.a: Switching routine breakroom, glass, and neutral floor chemistry to Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice concentrates adds only 0% to 4% to contract pricing while keeping indoor VOCs low. Any per-visit add-on—such as $15 to $30/restroom or $12 to $25/breakroom—multiplies by your exact monthly visit count (4.33 for weekly, 13.0 for 3x/week, or 21.65 for 5x/week based on 4.333 weeks/month).
